analysis: What changed versus the 8:00 AM brief: the rebound strengthened again rather than fading — the Dow went from +1.4% to +1.8% (900+ points), the S&P 500 from +1.7% to +1.9% and the Nasdaq from +2.1% to +2.2% by ~11:45 AM ET, with SOXX now +6%+ (from ~5%). The morning got two fresh megacap catalysts. JPMorgan's Analyst Focus List swap — Meta in, Alphabet out, Amazon alongside — is the day's cleanest rotation signal: it rests on a concrete thesis (Meta's Family of Apps ad revenue overtaking Google Search from Q4; AWS growth above 40% in 2027-28) and Meta's own Q3 numbers (ad revenue +26% to $63.1B), and it sent META and AMZN each ~5% higher while Alphabet still rose ~3%. Tesla's ~5.4% jump has a real driver too — robotaxi expansion to San Antonio, its eighth city, plus Musk reframing the Cybertruck wind-down as Cybercab capacity reallocation — but the China retail print (8,817 cars in October, lowest since July 2022, -66% YoY) is a genuine demand warning sitting under the rally, softened only by surging exports. Nvidia is unchanged in price (~-6%) but the story shifted to a waiting game: no timetable, no SEC filing, and the next hard dates are Nov 11 (House reply deadline), Nov 17 (earnings) and Nov 18 (briefing). The 11:00 AM ET NY Fed survey added the morning's only fresh macro data: inflation expectations flat at 3.9% (1-yr) — no new CPI worry — but job-market pessimism at its highest since April 2020, a soft-landing flag heading into Thursday's delayed jobs report. Signal vs noise: the JPMorgan rotation call, the chip rotation, the Tesla robotaxi expansion and the NY Fed survey are signal; Morgan Stanley's 8,000 year-end S&P target from the 8:00 AM brief remains supportive color; the Nvidia spy claims remain anonymous-source reporting with no public finding. The tape is still fragile — last week was the S&P's fourth straight weekly loss and its worst since April 2025, and a VIX near 23.5 says hedges are still on. Tuesday's CPI is the real checkpoint.

community_signals.takeaway: Now 893 points (up from 860 at the 8:00 AM brief). Discussion centers on whether the probe is a governance/leadership overhang or a buying opportunity in the underlying AI business, and on the unanswered question of what, if anything, was actually obtained — several top comments note the spy claims remain anonymous-source reporting with no public finding.

headlines.headline: The rebound kept strengthening into the late morning: the Dow was up 1.8% (900+ points), the S&P 500 +1.9% and the Nasdaq +2.2% as of ~11:45 AM ET, extending the bounce after the S&P's worst week since April 2025.
headlines.why_it_matters: Dip-buying is holding and broadening through the cash session rather than fading after the open — the recovery is now a full morning's move, though it follows a fourth straight weekly loss.

headlines.headline: JPMorgan added Meta to its Analyst Focus List, replacing Alphabet, and named Meta and Amazon its preferred internet picks: analyst Doug Anmuth expects Meta's Family of Apps advertising revenue to overtake Google Search revenue from the fourth quarter on AI-driven ad targeting, and sees AWS growth above 40% in 2027 and 2028. META rose ~5% to about $640 and AMZN ~5%; Alphabet still gained ~3% despite losing its spot. Meta's Q3 ad revenue rose 26% YoY to $63.1B.
headlines.why_it_matters: The day's clearest megacap catalyst — a top-bank rotation call with a concrete AI-ads thesis is pulling money into Meta and Amazon while Alphabet is demoted but not downgraded.

headlines.headline: Tesla jumped ~5.4% to about $377.55 after announcing robotaxi service starts in San Antonio this week (its eighth US city) with an expanded Austin coverage area, and Musk defended winding down Cybertruck production by mid-2027 to free Texas capacity for Cybercab, saying orders far exceed production. Counterweight: Tesla's October retail sales in China fell to 8,817 cars, the lowest since July 2022 and down 66% YoY, though surging exports lifted total China wholesale sales 10% YoY.
headlines.why_it_matters: Robotaxi expansion is the upside driver and Musk's Cybercab pivot reframes the Cybertruck wind-down as capacity reallocation, not failure — but the China retail collapse is a real demand warning sitting underneath the rally.

headlines.headline: Nvidia stayed down ~6% in late-morning action with no new development in the last hour: the board probe into CEO Jensen Huang has no published timetable and no SEC filing on the matter as of Monday; the stock is roughly 25-27% below its October high and about $270B of market value is at risk. NVDA reports Q3 earnings Nov 17 and Huang faces a closed-door House briefing Nov 18 (he must accept the date or offer another by Nov 11).
headlines.why_it_matters: The story is now a waiting game — with no deadline and no filing, the price action is about governance uncertainty and the silence between now and Nov 17, not any established fact; the spy claims remain anonymous-source reporting with no public finding.

headlines.headline: Chips rallied ex-Nvidia into the late morning: the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) jumped more than 6%, AMD was up 11% on Oppenheimer's upgrade to Outperform with a $600 target, Broadcom and Marvell each rose more than 8%, and Intel and Micron were solidly higher.
headlines.why_it_matters: Rotation within semis, not a sector exit — the AI-trade selloff is being priced as a Nvidia-specific governance problem while the rest of the chip complex rebounds.

headlines.headline: The NY Fed's October Survey of Consumer Expectations, released at 11:00 AM ET: one-year inflation expectations held steady at 3.9%, three-year at 3.3% and five-year at 3.0%, all matching September — still well above the Fed's 2% target. Expectations that the jobless rate will be higher a year from now hit their highest since April 2020.
headlines.why_it_matters: Steady inflation expectations give the Fed no new reason to flinch before Tuesday's CPI, but the sharpest job-market pessimism since the pandemic's early months is a soft-landing warning — it lands the same week the Fed is expected to hike in December.

headlines.headline: Oil stayed lower in the late morning: WTI crude futures were down 3.2% at $87.90 a barrel, near their lowest since late August, after President Trump said he was 'highly unlikely' to order further strikes on Iran as talks continued; Brent is down nearly 17% over the past week.
headlines.why_it_matters: Cheaper crude eases an inflation input a day before Tuesday's CPI and supports airlines and consumers — but gold's rise alongside stocks shows haven demand hasn't fully unwound.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC news this morning. Carried forward: record Q3 reported Nov 3 (revenue $357.2M, +43% YoY vs ~$348.32M consensus; Adjusted EBITDA $197.3M; DCF coverage 1.67x; EPS $0.33, in line), the $0.525 per-unit distribution paid Fri Nov 6 to holders of record Oct 26, and full-year guidance tightened to Adjusted EBITDA $770-780M and DCF $495-505M. Call color: over 60% of new horsepower scheduled for 2027 delivery is contracted (~90% of first-half deliveries); ~$500M order book through 2029; utilization slipped to 92.1% from 94.0%. New filing note: Alps Advisors raised its stake 15.5% in Q3 and now owns ~14.55% of the partnership. Management flagged cost pressure — monthly lubricant costs exited Q3 ~25% above first-half levels and diesel hit an all-time high in September. Cross-current today: WTI's slide to ~$87.90 pressures energy names broadly, though USAC's compression business is fee-based.

watch_next: Tue 8:30 a.m. ET: October CPI — the week's big checkpoint for the December hike debate (markets price roughly 70-80% odds of a 25bp hike after the hot payrolls print; consensus ~+0.3% m/m, core +0.2%).

Whether Nvidia's slide stays contained to NVDA or spreads — AMD, Broadcom, ASML and TSMC are all up, so rotation within semis is the live question; NVDA reports Q3 earnings Nov 17 and Huang faces a closed-door House briefing Nov 18 (he must accept the date or offer another by Nov 11).
After the close today: Take-Two, Occidental, Rocket Lab and The Trade Desk. Tue: Home Depot before the open, CoreWeave after the close.
